events.title: Prehistoric Hunter-Gatherer Societies
events.description: Archaeological evidence shows human activity in Côte d'Ivoire region during late Paleolithic period. Early inhabitants primarily engaged in hunting and gathering, using stone tools. These prehistoric groups seasonally migrated through forest and savanna zones, following game and gathering wild plants. Their lifestyle laid foundation for later sedentary agricultural societies.

events.title: Neolithic Revolution
events.description: Côte d'Ivoire region began experiencing early agricultural activity, marking transition from hunter-gatherer to farming society. Local inhabitants started domesticating indigenous crops like yams and oil palms. Pottery-making technology also emerged during this period, making food storage and cooking more convenient. Permanent villages began forming, population density gradually increased.

events.title: Early Settled Agriculture
events.description: More mature agricultural communities emerged in Côte d'Ivoire region, with residents cultivating multiple crops and raising livestock. Social organization during this period became more complex, with emergence of early social stratification. Archaeological sites show evidence of collective labor, such as large-scale forest clearing activities and early forms of irrigation systems.

events.title: Regional Trade Network Formation
events.description: Côte d'Ivoire region began establishing trade connections with neighboring areas, exchanging salt, stone tools, pottery and other goods. Salt production in coastal areas became important economic activity, while inland regions provided agricultural products and handicrafts. These early trade networks promoted cultural exchange and technology diffusion.

events.title: Early Bantu Migration
events.description: Bantu-speaking groups began migrating into present-day Côte d'Ivoire, bringing iron technology and agricultural knowledge. These early migrants established small villages, primarily engaged in farming and fishing. Their arrival marked the transition from Stone Age to Iron Age in the region, laying foundation for more complex social structures.

events.title: Iron Age Civilization
events.description: Côte d'Ivoire entered the Iron Age as local inhabitants mastered iron-working technology. Archaeological evidence shows emergence of advanced agricultural tools and weapons during this period. Use of iron promoted agricultural productivity, supporting population growth and emergence of more complex social organizations.

events.title: Trans-Saharan Trade Links
events.description: Northern Côte d'Ivoire began establishing connections with trans-Saharan trade networks. Local products like gold, ivory and kola nuts became important trade commodities, exchanged for salt, copper goods and other products from North Africa. These trade relationships promoted cultural exchange and economic development.

events.title: Early Kingdom Formation
events.description: Early political organizations and small kingdoms began emerging in Côte d'Ivoire. These kingdoms were mainly based on kinship relations and territorial alliances, controlling important trade routes and resources. Though small in scale, these early political entities provided foundation for later larger kingdom development.

events.title: Introduction of Islam
events.description: Through trans-Saharan trade, Islam began spreading to northern Côte d'Ivoire. Muslim merchants and scholars brought new religious beliefs, writing systems and commercial practices. Though Islam mainly spread in northern regions, it significantly influenced local culture and social structures.

events.title: Mande Migration
events.description: Mande ethnic groups from Mali Empire region began large-scale migration into northern Côte d'Ivoire. They brought advanced agricultural techniques, handicraft skills and political organizational forms. Mande arrival strengthened region's connections with West African inland empires, promoting cultural and economic development.

events.title: Mali Empire Influence
events.description: Powerful Mali Empire extended its influence to northern Côte d'Ivoire. Though not direct rule, Mali Empire controlled important trade routes and established trading posts in the region. This influence brought more advanced political systems, commercial practices and Islamic culture.

events.title: Akan Migration
events.description: Akan-speaking groups migrated from eastern regions into southeastern Côte d'Ivoire, establishing several small chiefdoms. Akan people brought complex political systems, gold mining techniques and unique cultural traditions. Their arrival enriched the region's ethnic composition and cultural diversity.

events.title: Kru Coastal Settlement
events.description: Kru ethnic groups established permanent settlements in Côte d'Ivoire's coastal regions. They developed advanced fishing techniques and maritime trading capabilities, becoming important maritime people of the region. Kru maritime skills later played important role during European colonial period.

events.title: Kong Kingdom Rise
events.description: Kong people established powerful kingdom in northern Côte d'Ivoire, controlling important trade routes. Kong Kingdom was renowned for its exquisite textile techniques and ironworking, becoming important political and economic force in the region. Kingdom established effective administrative system and military organization.

events.title: First Portuguese Arrival
events.description: Portuguese explorers first reached Côte d'Ivoire, beginning direct European contact with the region. Portuguese were mainly interested in ivory trade, which gave the region its name 'Ivory Coast.' Early European contact was mainly limited to coastal trade, with limited impact on inland areas.

events.title: Rise of Ivory Trade
events.description: European merchants began large-scale purchasing of ivory from Côte d'Ivoire, establishing regular trade relationships. Local chiefs and merchants organized ivory collection and trade, becoming important economic activity in the region. Ivory trade brought European goods, changing local material culture.

events.title: Multi-European Competition
events.description: Besides Portuguese, Dutch, British and French merchants also began establishing trading posts in Côte d'Ivoire. Various nations competed to control profitable ivory and gold trade. This competition led to complicated political landscape in coastal areas, with local rulers learning to exploit European competition for maximum benefit.

events.title: French Trading Post Established
events.description: France established its first permanent trading post at Assinie, marking beginning of French influence in Côte d'Ivoire. This trading post became base for French merchants to conduct ivory, gold and other commodity trade. French presence gradually strengthened, laying foundation for later colonial rule.

events.title: Beginning of Slave Trade
events.description: With increasing labor demand in American colonies, Côte d'Ivoire was also drawn into trans-Atlantic slave trade. Though scale was smaller than neighboring Gold Coast, significant numbers of locals were still sold into slavery. Slave trade profoundly impacted local social structures, intensifying inter-tribal conflicts.

events.title: Abron Kingdom Establishment
events.description: Abron people established their own kingdom in northeastern Côte d'Ivoire, with gold mining and trade as main economic activities. Abron Kingdom maintained complex relationship with Ashanti Empire, involving both cooperation and competition. Kingdom establishment promoted regional economic development and urbanization.

events.title: Baoulé Migration
events.description: Baoulé people migrated on large scale from Ghana region into central Côte d'Ivoire, establishing multiple chiefdoms. They brought advanced agricultural techniques and political organizational forms, becoming one of largest ethnic groups in the region. Baoulé arrival reshaped Côte d'Ivoire's ethnic landscape.

events.title: Senufo Kingdom Consolidation
events.description: Senufo people established stable political entity in northern Côte d'Ivoire, developing unique social organization and religious system. Senufo society was renowned for its exquisite artworks and mask carvings, while also being important agricultural producers. Their social organization profoundly influenced the region.

events.title: Ashanti Empire Influence
events.description: Powerful Ashanti Empire extended its influence to eastern Côte d'Ivoire. Ashanti controlled important trade routes and established alliance relationships with local rulers. This influence brought more advanced political systems and military technology, while intensifying regional political competition.

events.title: Dioula Merchant Network
events.description: Dioula Muslim merchants established extensive trade network connecting Côte d'Ivoire with West African inland regions. They played key role in trade of kola nuts, cloth and other commodities. Dioula merchants also spread Islam and Arabic script, promoting cultural exchange.

events.title: French Protection Treaties
events.description: France signed protection treaties with multiple coastal chiefs in Côte d'Ivoire, formally establishing French political influence in the region. These treaties nominally protected local rulers' authority but actually provided legal basis for French colonial expansion. Treaty signing marked beginning of Côte d'Ivoire's entry into French colonial era.

events.title: French Côte d'Ivoire Colony Established
events.description: France formally established French Côte d'Ivoire colony, with Louis Gustave Binger appointed as first governor. Colonial government began systematically controlling the region's political, economic and social life. France implemented direct rule policy, gradually weakening traditional chiefs' power.

events.title: Joining French West Africa
events.description: Côte d'Ivoire was incorporated into French West Africa federation, becoming its important component. This decision unified Côte d'Ivoire with other French West African colonies under single administration, promoting regional economic integration and administrative coordination. French West Africa establishment marked institutionalization of French colonial rule in West Africa.

events.title: Resistance Wars
events.description: Multiple armed resistances against French colonial rule erupted throughout Côte d'Ivoire. Most famous included Samori Touré's resistance movement and various chief-led uprisings. France deployed large military forces for suppression, finally establishing control over entire territory. Though these resistance movements failed, they became important spiritual legacy for later nationalist movements.

events.title: Forced Labor System
events.description: French colonial government implemented forced labor system, compelling locals to work for colonial infrastructure construction and plantations. This system seriously violated local people's human rights, causing massive deaths and social unrest. Forced labor system became one of most criticized aspects of colonial rule.

events.title: Dakar-Niger Railway
events.description: France began constructing railway connecting Dakar and Niger River, with Côte d'Ivoire becoming part of this important transportation network. Railway construction used massive forced labor, causing serious humanitarian problems. But railway also promoted economic development and regional integration.

events.title: Cocoa Plantation Development
events.description: French colonial government began vigorously promoting cocoa cultivation, with Côte d'Ivoire gradually becoming world's major cocoa producer. Cocoa cultivation changed the country's economic structure but also intensified land competition and social inequality. Cocoa economy development laid foundation for Côte d'Ivoire's later economic growth.

events.title: Abidjan Development
events.description: Abidjan began developing as Côte d'Ivoire's economic center, with port construction and urban planning making it important commercial hub of French West Africa. Large population migrated from rural areas to Abidjan seeking work opportunities, accelerating urbanization process. Abidjan's development changed the country's population distribution and social structure.

events.title: Bouaké Railway Completion
events.description: Railway connecting Abidjan and Bouaké was completed, greatly promoting economic links between inland regions and coast. Railway made transportation of cocoa, coffee and other agricultural products more convenient, but construction process used massive forced labor. This railway became important infrastructure for colonial economic development.

events.title: Great Depression Impact
events.description: Global Great Depression seriously affected Côte d'Ivoire's export economy, with cocoa and coffee prices plummeting. Colonial government was forced to adjust economic policies, reducing public spending and increasing taxes. Economic difficulties intensified local dissatisfaction with colonial rule, providing soil for later nationalist movements.

events.title: Upper Volta Annexed to Côte d'Ivoire
events.description: French colonial authorities annexed Upper Volta (present-day Burkina Faso) to Côte d'Ivoire colony to increase labor supply. This decision led to large numbers of Upper Volta people being forcibly relocated to work in Côte d'Ivoire's plantations. This administrative adjustment reflected colonial authorities' urgent need for labor.

events.title: Grand-Bassam Port Development
events.description: Grand-Bassam as early colonial capital and port continued developing, becoming important trade center. Although Abidjan gradually replaced its position, Grand-Bassam still played important role in export trade and colonial administration. City preserved many colonial-era buildings.

events.title: Vichy France Rule
events.description: After France's fall, Côte d'Ivoire was placed under Vichy France government rule. Vichy regime implemented even harsher colonial policies, strengthening control and exploitation of locals. This period's experiences deepened Ivorians' resentment toward French rule.

events.title: Free France Takeover
events.description: With Allied victory in North Africa, Free France government took over Côte d'Ivoire. New government promised colonial reforms, including abolishing forced labor and expanding local political participation. Though these promises were slowly implemented, they laid foundation for post-war political changes.

events.title: Brazzaville Conference
events.description: Côte d'Ivoire representatives participated in French colonial conference held in Brazzaville, discussing post-war colonial policy reforms. Conference decided to grant colonies more autonomy and promised gradual achievement of political equality. This conference marked important transformation in French colonial policy.

events.title: Félix Houphouët-Boigny's Rise
events.description: Félix Houphouët-Boigny became Côte d'Ivoire's most important political leader, founding Democratic Party of Côte d'Ivoire. He advocated achieving independence through peaceful means, opposing radical nationalism. Houphouët-Boigny's moderate line gained French support and laid foundation for Côte d'Ivoire's smooth transition.

events.title: French National Assembly Representation
events.description: Côte d'Ivoire gained representation in French National Assembly, with Houphouët-Boigny elected as deputy. This marked beginning of Ivorians' participation in French political decision-making process. Same year, forced labor system was formally abolished, important achievement of colonial reforms.

events.title: African Democratic Rally Founded
events.description: Houphouët-Boigny participated in founding African Democratic Rally, trans-colonial political organization aimed at fighting for African political rights. Organization initially allied with French Communist Party but later turned to moderate line. African Democratic Rally became most important political force in French Africa.

events.title: Planters' Association Establishment
events.description: African planters led by Houphouët-Boigny established their own association, fighting for economic equality with European planters. This organization became important foundation for Democratic Party of Côte d'Ivoire, representing interests of emerging African middle class. Association activities promoted colonial economic reforms.

events.title: Political Repression Period
events.description: French colonial authorities repressed African Democratic Rally, arresting many members and banning its activities. This repression caused casualties and political persecution but also sparked broader anti-colonial sentiment. This period's experiences strengthened nationalist movement's determination.

events.title: Break with Communist Party
events.description: Due to Cold War pressure and French government pressure, Houphouët-Boigny led African Democratic Rally to break with French Communist Party. This decision gained French government's trust but also caused dissatisfaction among party radicals. Break marked important transformation in Côte d'Ivoire's political line.

events.title: Coffee and Cocoa Stabilization Fund
events.description: Colonial government established Coffee and Cocoa Stabilization Fund to regulate agricultural price fluctuations. While supporting farmers' income, this fund also became tool for colonial government to control economy. Fund's operational methods caused dissatisfaction and controversy among African planters.

events.title: Loi-Cadre Framework
events.description: France passed Loi-Cadre framework law, granting French African colonies greater autonomy. Côte d'Ivoire gained internal autonomy status, establishing its own parliament and government. Houphouët-Boigny became government head, beginning preparation for eventual independence.

events.title: French Community Referendum
events.description: Côte d'Ivoire participated in referendum on joining French Community, voting overwhelmingly in favor. This decision granted Côte d'Ivoire greater autonomy while maintaining close ties with France. Referendum results reflected success of Houphouët-Boigny's moderate line.

events.title: Autonomous Republic
events.description: Côte d'Ivoire became autonomous republic within French Community, with Houphouët-Boigny as Prime Minister. New government began formulating post-independence development plans, including economic diversification and education expansion. Autonomous status provided valuable preparation time for complete independence.

events.title: Côte d'Ivoire Independence
events.description: Côte d'Ivoire formally declared independence, with Félix Houphouët-Boigny becoming first president. Independence was achieved through peaceful negotiations without armed struggle. New nation inherited relatively stable political system and economic foundation, laying good groundwork for later development.

events.title: UN Membership
events.description: Côte d'Ivoire joined United Nations, becoming formal member of international community. Also joined predecessor organizations of Organization of African Unity, actively participating in African affairs. International recognition provided important diplomatic support for Côte d'Ivoire's development.

events.title: Economic Miracle Begins
events.description: Côte d'Ivoire began rapid economic growth period called 'Ivorian Miracle.' Through developing agricultural exports and attracting foreign investment, national economy achieved 7-8% annual growth rate. Cocoa and coffee exports became economic pillars, with Abidjan developing as important commercial center in West Africa.

events.title: One-Party System Established
events.description: Houphouët-Boigny established one-party political system centered on Democratic Party of Côte d'Ivoire. Though limiting political pluralism, this system provided political stability in early independence period. One-party system lasted nearly 30 years, becoming important feature of Côte d'Ivoire's political development.

events.title: University of Abidjan Founded
events.description: University of Abidjan (now University of Cocody) was established, becoming Côte d'Ivoire's flagship higher education institution. University establishment marked nation's emphasis on educational development, laying foundation for cultivating local talent. University of Abidjan also became important academic center in Francophone Africa.

events.title: Economic Diversification
events.description: Côte d'Ivoire began promoting economic diversification policy, developing manufacturing and service industries. Government established multiple industrial parks, attracting foreign investment for factory establishment. Though agriculture remained economic mainstay, industrial sector development laid foundation for economic structural adjustment.

events.title: Ivoirianization Policy
events.description: Government launched Ivoirianization policy, requiring foreign companies to employ more local staff and transfer technology. This policy aimed to reduce dependence on foreign experts and improve local employment opportunities and skill levels. Policy achieved some success but also faced implementation difficulties.

events.title: West African Economic and Monetary Union
events.description: Côte d'Ivoire became founding member of West African Economic and Monetary Union, adopting West African CFA franc as common currency. This decision strengthened economic integration with neighboring countries but also limited monetary policy independence. Union provided convenience for regional trade and investment.

events.title: Economic Crisis Begins
events.description: Due to declining cocoa and coffee prices, plus oil crisis impact, Côte d'Ivoire's economy began facing difficulties. Government debt increased sharply, economic growth slowed. This marked end of 'Ivorian Miracle,' with nation beginning to face serious economic challenges.

events.title: Capital Moved to Yamoussoukro
events.description: Houphouët-Boigny announced moving capital from Abidjan to his hometown Yamoussoukro. This decision caused controversy, criticized as resource waste. Though Yamoussoukro became political capital, Abidjan remained economic center.

events.title: Structural Adjustment Program
events.description: Under World Bank and IMF pressure, Côte d'Ivoire began implementing structural adjustment program. Program included reducing government spending, privatizing state enterprises and trade liberalization. Though helpful for economic stability, it also caused social difficulties and increased inequality.

events.title: Basilica of Our Lady of Peace Completed
events.description: Basilica of Our Lady of Peace in Yamoussoukro was completed, becoming one of world's largest Christian churches. This costly building reflected Houphouët-Boigny's personal ambition but also drew criticism about resource allocation. Basilica became important landmark of Côte d'Ivoire.

events.title: Multi-Party Reform
events.description: Facing domestic and international pressure, Houphouët-Boigny announced multi-party system reform. New constitution allowed legal existence of opposition parties and promised multi-party elections. This reform marked major transformation in Côte d'Ivoire's political system, ending 30 years of one-party rule.

events.title: First Multi-Party Election
events.description: Côte d'Ivoire held first multi-party presidential election since independence, with Houphouët-Boigny winning 81% of votes. Though election process was controversial, it marked beginning of political pluralization. Opposition party participation provided new platform for political competition.

events.title: Houphouët-Boigny's Death
events.description: Côte d'Ivoire's founding father Félix Houphouët-Boigny died, ending 33 years of rule. His death marked end of an era and brought uncertainty to national political development. Houphouët-Boigny was hailed as architect of modern Côte d'Ivoire.

events.title: Bédié Succeeds as President
events.description: National Assembly Speaker Henri Konan Bédié succeeded as president according to constitution. Bédié was close ally of Houphouët-Boigny, promising to continue predecessor's policies. His succession provided guarantee for political stability but also faced economic difficulties and political challenges.

events.title: Controversial Presidential Election
events.description: Bédié won controversial presidential election, with main opposition candidates disqualified from participation. Election results drew international criticism and domestic political tension. This election exposed fragility of Côte d'Ivoire's democratic system.

events.title: Military Coup
events.description: General Robert Guéï led military coup, overthrowing Bédié government. Coup reasons included economic difficulties, military pay issues and political corruption. This was Côte d'Ivoire's first military coup since independence, marking end of political stability era.

events.title: New Constitution Referendum
events.description: Military government held new constitution referendum, introducing controversial 'Ivoirité' concept requiring presidential candidates' parents both be Ivorian-born. This clause was considered discriminatory measure against northern Muslim population, intensifying ethnic and religious tensions.

events.title: Gbagbo Elected President
events.description: Laurent Gbagbo won controversial presidential election, with main opposition candidate Alassane Ouattara banned from participation. Post-election violence erupted, causing hundreds of deaths. Gbagbo's election intensified national political divisions.

events.title: Civil War Outbreak
events.description: Côte d'Ivoire civil war erupted, with rebel 'Patriotic Movement' controlling northern regions. War roots included political exclusion, economic inequality and ethnic-religious contradictions. War led to national division into north and south, causing massive casualties and refugees.

events.title: Linas-Marcoussis Agreement
events.description: Under international mediation, warring parties signed Linas-Marcoussis peace agreement, establishing government of national unity. Agreement stipulated power-sharing and gradual national reunification. Though temporarily stopping fighting, agreement implementation was difficult with peace process repeatedly stalled.

events.title: French Military Intervention
events.description: After Ivorian air force bombed French military base, France launched 'Operation Unicorn,' destroying Ivorian air force. French intervention triggered anti-French demonstrations and violence, with massive French expatriate evacuation. This event seriously damaged Franco-Ivorian relations, intensifying domestic tensions.

events.title: UN Peacekeeping Deployment
events.description: UN Operation in Côte d'Ivoire (UNOCI) formally deployed, jointly maintaining ceasefire with French forces. Peacekeepers operated in confidence zone separating north and south, providing guarantee for peace process. International community intervention played important role in stabilizing situation.

events.title: Ouagadougou Agreement
events.description: President Gbagbo and opposition leader Soro signed Ouagadougou Agreement, restarting peace process. Agreement included disarmament, voter registration and holding elections. Though progress was slow, agreement provided framework for eventual crisis resolution.

events.title: Presidential Election Crisis
events.description: Côte d'Ivoire held long-delayed presidential election, with both Ouattara and Gbagbo claiming victory. International community recognized Ouattara's victory, but Gbagbo refused to cede power. Election dispute triggered new round of political crisis and violent conflicts, with nation again divided.

events.title: Gbagbo's Arrest
events.description: With French and UN forces support, Ouattara's army captured Abidjan, with Gbagbo arrested at presidential palace. Gbagbo's arrest ended four-month post-election crisis, with Ouattara formally assuming presidency. This marked beginning of new era for Côte d'Ivoire.

events.title: Post-Election Crisis
events.description: Gbagbo's refusal to recognize election results led to serious political and humanitarian crisis. Conflict caused about 3,000 deaths and 1 million displaced persons. International community imposed sanctions on Gbagbo, supporting Ouattara government. Crisis lasted months, seriously undermining national stability.

events.title: Ouattara's Inauguration
events.description: Alassane Ouattara formally assumed Côte d'Ivoire presidency, promising national reconciliation and reconstruction. New government faced enormous challenges including restoring national unity, rebuilding economy and judicial system. Ouattara's inauguration opened new chapter for national peaceful development.

events.title: Truth and Reconciliation Commission
events.description: Government established Truth and Reconciliation Commission to investigate violence during 2002-2011 crisis. Commission aimed to promote national reconciliation and provide justice for victims. Though work faced challenges, it provided important platform for national healing.

events.title: Economic Recovery Begins
events.description: Côte d'Ivoire's economy began strong recovery with GDP growth rate exceeding 9%. Government launched large-scale infrastructure construction program, attracting foreign investment return. Rising cocoa prices and political stability provided favorable conditions for economic recovery.

events.title: Gbagbo Transferred to ICC
events.description: Former President Gbagbo was transferred to International Criminal Court in The Hague, facing crimes against humanity charges. This was first time African former head of state tried at ICC, with important legal and political significance. Trial process received close international attention.

events.title: New Constitution Adopted
events.description: Côte d'Ivoire adopted new constitution, establishing vice-presidency and limiting presidential terms. New constitution aimed to strengthen democratic system and prevent excessive power concentration. Constitutional reform laid legal foundation for political system modernization.

events.title: Ouattara Re-elected
events.description: Ouattara won presidential election re-election with overwhelming majority, receiving over 80% of votes. Election process was relatively peaceful, with international observers considering election free and fair. Ouattara's re-election provided political stability for continuing national development.

events.title: Grand-Bassam Terror Attack
events.description: Islamic extremists launched terrorist attack in coastal resort city Grand-Bassam, killing 19 people. This was Côte d'Ivoire's first international terrorism attack, exposing security vulnerabilities. Government strengthened counter-terrorism measures and international cooperation.

events.title: Military Mutiny
events.description: Military mutinies erupted in multiple Côte d'Ivoire locations, with soldiers demanding pay raises and improved treatment. Government reached agreement with mutinous soldiers, promising improved military treatment. Mutiny exposed necessity of military reform and social dissatisfaction.

events.title: Gbagbo Acquitted
events.description: International Criminal Court announced Laurent Gbagbo's acquittal, though prosecution appealed. Gbagbo's release caused complex reactions in Côte d'Ivoire, with supporters celebrating and opponents worried. This event significantly impacted domestic politics.

events.title: Bédié Returns to Politics
events.description: Former President Henri Konan Bédié announced return to politics, resuming leadership of Democratic Party of Côte d'Ivoire. Bédié's return changed political landscape, adding variables to 2020 presidential election. His return also symbolized progress in political reconciliation.

events.title: Controversial Presidential Election
events.description: Côte d'Ivoire held presidential election with Ouattara winning third term. Main opposition parties boycotted election, resulting in low turnout. Pre- and post-election violence caused dozens of deaths. International community was divided on election legitimacy.

events.title: Ouattara Announces Third Term Bid
events.description: Ouattara announced candidacy for third presidential term, causing constitutional controversy and political tension. Opposition considered this violated constitutional two-term limit. Ouattara's decision reignited political divisions, casting shadow over election.

events.title: Political Reconciliation Efforts
events.description: President Ouattara held dialogue with main opposition leaders, working to ease political tensions. Government released some political prisoners and promised judicial reforms. Though reconciliation process was slow, it provided hope for political stability.

events.title: Parliamentary Elections
events.description: Côte d'Ivoire held National Assembly elections with ruling party winning majority seats. Opposition parties partially participated in election, improving political participation. Elections proceeded relatively peacefully, taking important step toward political normalization.

events.title: Economic Challenges
events.description: Côte d'Ivoire faced economic challenges including rising inflation and increasing debt. COVID-19 pandemic and Russia-Ukraine war impacted economy, with government introducing response measures. Despite difficulties, economy maintained relatively stable growth.

events.title: Local Elections
events.description: Côte d'Ivoire held local elections, further advancing democratization process. Elections strengthened local governance and improved citizen political participation. Though some problems existed, elections generally proceeded peacefully.

events.title: Vision 2030 Plan
events.description: Government launched 'Côte d'Ivoire Vision 2030' development plan, aiming to achieve economic transformation and social development. Plan focuses on developing manufacturing, digital economy and infrastructure. This ambitious plan outlined blueprint for national future development. Côte d'Ivoire continues efforts to consolidate democratic system, achieve sustainable development, and play greater role in regional affairs. Despite facing challenges, nation is moving toward more prosperous and stable future.
